sentences.text: Heard Mr. I. Haque, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms. M. D. Borah, learned Standing Counsel for the Transport Department.

2. The present writ petition is filed assailing inaction on the part of the State Government in bringing out the necessary Notification pursuant to the direction Page No.# 3/4 passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Usha Devi -Vs- Pawan Kumar reported in 2008 SCC 1602.
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The other issue involves in this petition is as regards the implementation of Rule 8 of the Inter-Country Transport Vehicles Rules, 2021, which prescribes the necessity for insurance against Sanjila Brahma vs The State Of Assam And 5 Ors on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62503946/
2 3rd party risk, inasmuch as, in the present case, the daughter of the petitioner died in a motor vehicle accident involving a Bhutanese vehicle.

entities.text: Sanjila Brahma vs The State Of Assam And 5 Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the another issue also involves as regards the implementation of Section 148 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, which deals with the validity of policies of insurance issued in reciprocating countries.

4. Mr. Haque, learned counsel for the petitioner also argues that even otherwise, the petitioner is entitled for ex-gratia compensation in terms of Notification No. E.2922332/2 dated 31.10.2023,
more particularly, for the reason that it is the responsibility of the State to ensure that no uninsured vehicle of foreign country enters into the State and therefore, for failure on the part of the State authority, the victim/mother is entitled to compensation.
5.

It is his further case that such compensation is required to be determined in terms of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Hitesh Nagjibhai Patel -Vs- Bababhai Nagjibhai Rabari & Anr.
reported in (2025) LiveLaw (SC) 871.
6.

entities.text: Hitesh Nagjibhai Patel -Vs- Bababhai Nagjibhai Rabari & Anr.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this stage, Ms. Borah, learned Standing Counsel for the Transport Department submits that after verification, the Transport Department being satisfied, has sent a proposal to the District Commissioner, Baksa, BTAD for consideration of the case of the petitioner under the Notification dated 31.10.2023.

7. That being the position, keeping the arguments raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner for consideration on the next date fixed, it is directed that the Page No.# 4/4 District Commissioner,
Baksa, BTAD i.e. the respondent No. 4, shall consider the proposal forwarded by the Commissioner of Transport Department and a decision be taken within a period of four weeks from receipt of a certified copy of this order to be furnished by the petitioner.
8.

The petitioner may furnish a copy of this order passed today before the District Commissioner,
Baksa, BTAD, within a period of ten days from today.
If any further documentation is required, the petitioner shall duly assist the District Commissioner by furnishing the same.
9. List this matter on 28.11.2025.
